title: Felix and the Vow
premise: Ansel Vasquez, widowed single parent and owner of the failing Last Chapter bookshop, agrees to a fake date with Felix Marsh — a charming stranger he meets by chance — to survive his meddling family's reunion. What begins as an arrangement becomes real, until Ansel discovers Felix is the investigator whose testimony could doom the bakery downstairs, the livelihood of Marisol, the grandmother who helped raise Ansel's daughter. Caught between a decade-old vow to protect his found family and a love he never expected, Ansel must publicly testify about the corrupt land deal he witnessed as a teenager — the sentence he has rehearsed for ten years — before the bakery lease runs out. In the end, truth saves the bakery, Felix chooses Ansel over his employer, and the family they built around a bookshop counter becomes permanent.
about_author: Astrid Winterbourne is a former small-town librarian who writes romances about people who rebuild their lives one stubborn act of kindness at a time. She lives in a coastal village with her partner, two cats, and an ever-growing stack of annotated paperbacks.

chapters.title: The Last Chapter
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet Ansel balancing ledgers, his daughter Lucia's homework, and the bakery smell drifting up from Marisol's shop below. The lease renewal letter arrives with a 60-day deadline. Beat: weary tenderness, the quiet fear that everything he's built is slipping.

chapters.title: Stranger at the Poetry Shelf
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix ducks into the bookshop to escape a tail — a corporate investigator scouting the block for his firm's client. He and Ansel banter over a battered Neruda collection. Beat: instant, disarming chemistry that Felix refuses to examine too closely.

chapters.title: The Reunion Summons
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel's sister Rosa calls: the annual family reunion, where everyone will ask why he's still alone ten years after his husband's death. Lucia, overhearing, innocently wishes he had someone to bring. Beat: grief resurfacing as obligation; the fake-date idea sparks.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix returns to buy the Neruda and finds Ansel drafting a desperate 'plus-one wanted' note. He offers himself, joking, then means it — he needs cover too, from a colleague who reads too much into his evenings. Beat: a deal struck with laughter hiding mutual loneliness.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner for Liars
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. First rehearsal: coffee, backstory rules, three facts each. Felix's invented childhood is suspiciously polished; Ansel's is too sparse. Lucia walks in and instantly adopts Felix. Beat: warmth creeping past the contract's fine print.

chapters.title: The Vasquez Gauntlet
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The reunion's first day: Rosa's interrogations, Tío Bruno's chess ambush, Lucia proudly showing Felix her bookshelf. Felix plays the part so well it frightens him. Beat: belonging as an intoxicant; the first crack in his professional detachment.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Dessert, dancing under string lights, a kiss staged for the aunts that neither pulls back from. Ansel flees to the porch, shaken; Felix follows and they almost tell the truth. Beat: the fake date collapses into something terrifyingly genuine.

chapters.title: What Felix Knows
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Back at his hotel, Felix reviews his actual assignment: his firm is building the case to buy out the block — the bakery included — and needs testimony that the current owner's claim is shaky. He realizes Ansel's family is the target. Beat: guilt arriving ahead of confession.

chapters.title: Marisol's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sunday bread with Marisol, who reveals the lease pressure and a developer's lowball offer, and mentions a 'nice young man' who asked odd questions about the property's history. Ansel's stomach drops. Beat: dread threading through domestic comfort.

chapters.title: The Vow, Explained
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback-heavy. Ten years ago, teenage Ansel witnessed the land deal that cheated Marisol's late husband; he promised her he'd never speak of it, fearing retaliation that could cost him custody of Lucia. Beat: the weight of a vow made by a frightened kid.

chapters.title: Dates That Aren't Dates
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A montage of 'practice' dates — the pier, a used-record fair, Lucia's school play — that fool no one, least of themselves. Each closes on a near-confession interrupted. Beat: falling in love while both hide a secret.

chapters.title: The Colleague
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix's coworker Dana corners him: the client wants the bakery's file expedited, and she's noticed Felix's local entanglements. Felix stalls, then deletes a damaging memo. Beat: the point of no return — he's chosen a side without admitting it.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel finds Felix's dropped case folder in the bookshop: the buyout plan, his name on it. He reads everything, then says nothing, testing Felix over dinner. Beat: betrayal and hope in the same breath — Felix lies badly, and Ansel lets him.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel finally confronts Felix among the shelves after close. Felix confesses all — the assignment, the deleted memo, the feelings. Ansel, raw, orders him out. Beat: the midpoint rupture; both truths on the table, neither forgiven.

chapters.title: Sixty Days Become Twelve
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix resigns, burning his professional bridge, and starts pulling the real records of the original land deal from county archives. Dana warns him the client will retaliate. Beat: Felix converting guilt into action, at real cost.

chapters.title: What Lucia Saw
chapters.summary: Lucia's POV (via Ansel). Lucia, hurt by the shouting she overheard, asks Ansel if Felix is gone like Papá is gone. Ansel realizes his silence — the vow — has taught his daughter to expect abandonment. Beat: the vow's true price made visible through a child.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Marisol, learning everything, releases Ansel from the vow — 'I never wanted your silence, mijo, I wanted you safe.' Ansel writes the sentence he's rehearsed for a decade and reads it aloud to Lucia first. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the emergency lease/land-use hearing, Felix presents the archived records; the developer's lawyer attacks his credibility. Then Ansel takes the stand and speaks the rehearsed sentence — naming the men, the deal, the decade of silence. Beat: the climax; justice seized outside the law's comfort.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Ash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They win the stay, but Felix's career is ash and he assumes he should leave town before he costs Ansel more. Rosa and the aunts, having watched everything, stage an intervention of casseroles and blunt questions. Beat: the found family claiming Felix before he can vanish.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Lease day: Marisol signs a new ten-year lease backed by a community fund the family organized. Ansel finds Felix packing at his motel and finally says the other rehearsed sentence — the one about love, in present tense. Beat: the second vow, freely made.

chapters.title: Shelving a Future
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Weeks later: Felix works the bookshop register badly and happily, Lucia assigns him a reading list, and the Neruda gets a permanent place by the register. Beat: ordinary joy earned the hard way.

chapters.title: Felix and the Vow
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. One year on: the reunion again, but this time no one asks why Ansel is alone. He toasts the family — blood and chosen — and privately revisits the old vow, rewriting it into a promise kept. Beat: full-circle resolution; love moved from past tense to future.
